newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable, mid distillate trade lulled.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable, mid distillate trade lulled.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha held steady on Thursday with no fresh incentives heard from overseas markets, while activity in spot middle distillate trades remained extremely quiet amid high domestic stockpiles, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half August was quoted at $214.50/215.50 per tonne after having been traded at $215.00.
In inter-delivery spreads, first-half August/second-half August was traded at plus 30 cents.
Naphtha spreads from first-half August onwards are expected to remain in backwardation as long as the arbitrage window from the West is closed, traders said.
Demand for middle distillate import cargoes are virtually non-existent due to high domestic stockpiles, traders said.
Kerosene and gas oil stocks at the end of April were up 50 percent and 24 percent, respectively, from a year ago, and are believed to have remained high since, traders said.
"With middle distillate stocks this high, spot imports are just prohibitive," one trader with a refiner said.
As oil firms are usually reluctant to lower refinery utilisation rates, spot imports are the first to be eliminated in a bid to reduce inventories, traders said.
